note: Original problems written for TEMS Academy. They are not past examination questions.

problems.subject: mathematics
problems.title: Last digit of a power
problems.statement: Find the last digit of $7^{2026}$.
problems.hint: The last digits of powers of $7$ repeat in a cycle of four: $7,9,3,1$.
problems.solution: The cycle has length $4$. Since $2026\equiv2\pmod4$, the last digit is the second entry in the cycle, which is $9$.

problems.subject: mathematics
problems.title: Digits that add to nine
problems.statement: How many two-digit positive integers have digits that add up to $9$?
problems.hint: Let the tens digit be $a\in\{1,2,\dots,9\}$. Then the units digit is $9-a$.
problems.solution: For each tens digit $a=1,2,\dots,9$, the units digit $9-a$ lies between $0$ and $8$, so it is valid. Hence there are $9$ such numbers: $18,27,36,\dots,90$.

problems.subject: mathematics
problems.title: Hands at half past three
problems.statement: What is the smaller angle between the hour hand and the minute hand at $3{:}30$?
problems.hint: The minute hand points at $6$. The hour hand has moved half an hour-mark past $3$.
problems.solution: At $3{:}30$ the minute hand is at $180^\circ$ from $12$. The hour hand is at $3.5$ hour-marks, which is $3.5\times30^\circ=105^\circ$. The difference is $180^\circ-105^\circ=75^\circ$.

problems.subject: mathematics
problems.title: A power modulo seven
problems.statement: Find the remainder when $3^{100}$ is divided by $7$.
problems.hint: Compute the powers of $3$ modulo $7$ until the sequence repeats.
problems.solution: Modulo $7$: $3^1\equiv3$, $3^2\equiv2$, $3^3\equiv6$, $3^4\equiv4$, $3^5\equiv5$, $3^6\equiv1$. The cycle has length $6$, and $100\equiv4\pmod6$, so $3^{100}\equiv3^4\equiv4\pmod7$.

problems.subject: mathematics
problems.title: Three primes in a row
problems.statement: Find all primes $p$ such that $p$, $p+2$ and $p+4$ are all prime.
problems.hint: Consider the three numbers modulo $3$.
problems.solution: If $p\neq3$, then $p\equiv1$ or $2\pmod3$. If $p\equiv1\pmod3$, then $p+2\equiv0\pmod3$; if $p\equiv2\pmod3$, then $p+4\equiv0\pmod3$. In either case one of the three numbers is a multiple of $3$ larger than $3$, hence composite. For $p=3$, the numbers are $3,5,7$, all prime. Thus $p=3$ is the only solution.

problems.subject: mathematics
problems.title: Area from three sides
problems.statement: A triangle has sides $7$, $24$ and $25$. Find its area.
problems.hint: Check whether the triangle is right-angled.
problems.solution: $7^2+24^2=49+576=625=25^2$, so the triangle is right-angled with legs $7$ and $24$. Its area is $\tfrac12\cdot7\cdot24=84$.

problems.subject: mathematics
problems.title: Unit fractions
problems.statement: Find the number of ordered pairs $(x,y)$ of positive integers satisfying $\dfrac1x+\dfrac1y=\dfrac16$.
problems.hint: Multiply by $6xy$ and factor: $(x-6)(y-6)=36$.
problems.solution: From $\frac1x+\frac1y=\frac16$ we get $6y+6x=xy$, so $xy-6x-6y=0$ and therefore $(x-6)(y-6)=36$. For positive integers $x,y$ we need $x>6$ and $y>6$. Each positive divisor $d$ of $36$ gives one pair $x=6+d$, $y=6+36/d$. Since $36$ has $9$ positive divisors, there are $9$ ordered pairs.

problems.subject: mathematics
problems.title: Divisibility by thirty
problems.statement: Prove that $n^5-n$ is divisible by $30$ for every integer $n$.
problems.hint: Show divisibility by $2$, $3$ and $5$ separately, or factor $n^5-n$.
problems.solution: $n^5-n=n(n^4-1)=n(n-1)(n+1)(n^2+1)$. Among the three consecutive integers $n-1,n,n+1$, one is divisible by $3$ and at least one is even, so the product is divisible by $6$. For divisibility by $5$: if $n\equiv0,\pm1\pmod5$, then one of $n,n-1,n+1$ is divisible by $5$; if $n\equiv\pm2\pmod5$, then $n^2+1\equiv4+1\equiv0\pmod5$. Hence the product is divisible by $2\cdot3\cdot5=30$.

problems.subject: physics
problems.title: Average speed
problems.statement: A runner covers $120\ \text{m}$ in $15\ \text{s}$. What is the average speed?
problems.hint: Average speed is total distance divided by total time.
problems.solution: $v=\dfrac{d}{t}=\dfrac{120\ \text{m}}{15\ \text{s}}=8\ \text{m s}^{-1}$.

problems.subject: physics
problems.title: Density of a block
problems.statement: A block has mass $240\ \text{g}$ and volume $30\ \text{cm}^3$. Find its density.
problems.hint: Density is mass per unit volume.
problems.solution: $\rho=\dfrac{m}{V}=\dfrac{240\ \text{g}}{30\ \text{cm}^3}=8\ \text{g cm}^{-3}$.

problems.subject: physics
problems.title: Two resistors in series
problems.statement: Resistors of $6\ \Omega$ and $3\ \Omega$ are connected in series across an $18\ \text{V}$ supply. Find the current.
problems.hint: In series, the resistances add.
problems.solution: $R=6+3=9\ \Omega$, so $I=\dfrac{V}{R}=\dfrac{18}{9}=2\ \text{A}$.

problems.subject: physics
problems.title: Projectile from a height
problems.statement: A ball is thrown horizontally at $20\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ from a height of $45\ \text{m}$. Taking $g=10\ \text{m s}^{-2}$, find the horizontal range.
problems.hint: First find the time to fall $45\ \text{m}$ from rest vertically.
problems.solution: Vertical motion: $45=\tfrac12\cdot10\cdot t^2$, so $t=3\ \text{s}$. Horizontal range: $x=20\cdot3=60\ \text{m}$.

problems.subject: physics
problems.title: Parallel then series
problems.statement: Two $4\ \Omega$ resistors are connected in parallel, and the combination is connected in series with a $3\ \Omega$ resistor across a $10\ \text{V}$ supply. Find the total current.
problems.hint: Find the equivalent resistance of the parallel pair first.
problems.solution: The parallel pair has resistance $\dfrac{4\cdot4}{4+4}=2\ \Omega$. The total resistance is $2+3=5\ \Omega$, so $I=\dfrac{10}{5}=2\ \text{A}$.

problems.subject: physics
problems.title: Image from a convex lens
problems.statement: An object is placed $15\ \text{cm}$ from a convex lens of focal length $10\ \text{cm}$. Find the image distance and magnification.
problems.hint: Use $\dfrac1f=\dfrac1v-\dfrac1u$ with the sign convention you have been taught, or use the real-object form $\dfrac1f=\dfrac1u+\dfrac1v$.
problems.solution: Using the real-object form, $\dfrac1v=\dfrac1f-\dfrac1u=\dfrac1{10}-\dfrac1{15}=\dfrac1{30}$, so $v=30\ \text{cm}$. The magnification is $m=\dfrac{v}{u}=2$, so the image is real, inverted and twice the size.

problems.subject: physics
problems.title: Carnot efficiency
problems.statement: A Carnot engine operates between a hot reservoir at $500\ \text{K}$ and a cold reservoir at $300\ \text{K}$. Find its efficiency.
problems.hint: For a Carnot engine, $\eta=1-\dfrac{T_C}{T_H}$ with temperatures in kelvin.
problems.solution: $\eta=1-\dfrac{300}{500}=1-0.6=0.4$, so the efficiency is $40\%$.

problems.subject: physics
problems.title: Pressure drop in a narrowing pipe
problems.statement: Water flows steadily through a horizontal pipe that narrows from cross-sectional area $4\ \text{cm}^2$ to $1\ \text{cm}^2$. The speed in the wider section is $1\ \text{m s}^{-1}$. Taking the density of water as $1000\ \text{kg m}^{-3}$, find the pressure drop between the two sections.
problems.hint: Use continuity to find the speed in the narrow section, then Bernoulli’s equation.
problems.solution: Continuity gives $A_1v_1=A_2v_2$, so $v_2=4\ \text{m s}^{-1}$. Bernoulli along the horizontal pipe gives $p_1-p_2=\tfrac12\rho(v_2^2-v_1^2)=\tfrac12(1000)(16-1)=7500\ \text{Pa}$.

problems.subject: chemistry
problems.title: Moles in a glass of water
problems.statement: How many moles are in $18\ \text{g}$ of water? Take $M(\text{H}_2\text{O})=18\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$.
problems.hint: Use $n=\dfrac{m}{M}$.
problems.solution: $n=\dfrac{18}{18}=1\ \text{mol}$. This contains $6.022\times10^{23}$ water molecules.

problems.subject: chemistry
problems.title: pH of a strong acid
problems.statement: Find the pH of a $0.01\ \text{mol dm}^{-3}$ solution of hydrochloric acid.
problems.hint: HCl is a strong acid, so it dissociates completely.

problems.subject: chemistry
problems.title: Particles in sodium-23
problems.statement: How many protons and neutrons are in a ${}^{23}\text{Na}$ atom?
problems.hint: Sodium has atomic number $11$.
problems.solution: The atomic number is $11$, so there are $11$ protons. The mass number is $23$, so the number of neutrons is $23-11=12$.

problems.subject: chemistry
problems.title: Molarity of sodium hydroxide
problems.statement: $4.0\ \text{g}$ of NaOH is dissolved in water to make $500\ \text{cm}^3$ of solution. Find the molarity. Take $M(\text{NaOH})=40\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$.
problems.hint: Find moles first, then divide by volume in $\text{dm}^3$.
problems.solution: $n=\dfrac{4.0}{40}=0.10\ \text{mol}$. The volume is $0.500\ \text{dm}^3$, so $c=\dfrac{0.10}{0.500}=0.20\ \text{mol dm}^{-3}$.

problems.subject: chemistry
problems.title: Water from hydrogen
problems.statement: For the reaction $2\text{H}_2+\text{O}_2\to2\text{H}_2\text{O}$, $4\ \text{mol}$ of hydrogen reacts with excess oxygen. What mass of water is formed? Take $M(\text{H}_2\text{O})=18\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$.
problems.hint: Use the stoichiometric ratio from the balanced equation.
problems.solution: The equation gives $2\ \text{mol}$ of water for every $2\ \text{mol}$ of hydrogen, so $4\ \text{mol}$ of hydrogen gives $4\ \text{mol}$ of water. The mass is $4\times18=72\ \text{g}$.

problems.subject: chemistry
problems.title: Empirical formula
problems.statement: A compound contains $40.0\%$ carbon, $6.7\%$ hydrogen and $53.3\%$ oxygen by mass. Find its empirical formula.
problems.hint: Divide each percentage by the relative atomic mass, then divide by the smallest result.
problems.solution: Moles per $100\ \text{g}$: C $=40.0/12=3.33$, H $=6.7/1=6.7$, O $=53.3/16=3.33$. Dividing by $3.33$ gives C:H:O $=1:2:1$, so the empirical formula is $\text{CH}_2\text{O}$.

problems.subject: chemistry
problems.title: Equilibrium constant
problems.statement: For $\text{A}\rightleftharpoons\text{B}$, the initial concentration of A is $1.0\ \text{mol dm}^{-3}$ and no B is present. At equilibrium, $[\text{B}]=0.20\ \text{mol dm}^{-3}$. Find $K_c$.
problems.hint: Use an ICE table: the amount of A that reacted equals the amount of B formed.
problems.solution: At equilibrium $[\text{B}]=0.20$, so $0.20\ \text{mol dm}^{-3}$ of A reacted and $[\text{A}]=1.0-0.20=0.80\ \text{mol dm}^{-3}$. Hence $K_c=\dfrac{[\text{B}]}{[\text{A}]}=\dfrac{0.20}{0.80}=0.25$.

problems.subject: chemistry
problems.title: First-order half-life
problems.statement: A first-order reaction has a half-life of $10\ \text{min}$. What fraction of the reactant remains after $30\ \text{min}$?
problems.hint: Each half-life halves the remaining amount.
problems.solution: After $10$, $20$ and $30\ \text{min}$ the amount is halved three times: $\left(\tfrac12\right)^3=\tfrac18$. So $\tfrac18$ of the reactant remains.

problems.subject: biology
problems.title: The cell’s power station
problems.statement: Which organelle is the main site of aerobic respiration in a eukaryotic cell?
problems.hint: It has a double membrane and its own DNA.
problems.solution: The mitochondrion is the main site of aerobic respiration. Its inner membrane hosts the electron transport chain that produces most of the cell’s ATP.

problems.subject: biology
problems.title: A simple cross
problems.statement: In a species where $A$ is dominant over $a$, a plant of genotype $AA$ is crossed with a plant of genotype $aa$. What genotypes will the offspring have?
problems.hint: Each parent contributes one allele.
problems.solution: The $AA$ parent can contribute only $A$, and the $aa$ parent can contribute only $a$. Every offspring therefore receives $A$ from one parent and $a$ from the other, giving genotype $Aa$.

problems.subject: biology
problems.title: Universal donor
problems.statement: Which ABO/Rh blood type is called the universal donor for red blood cells?
problems.hint: It has neither A nor B antigens and no Rh D antigen.
problems.solution: O negative blood has no A, B or Rh D antigens on the red cells, so it can be given to recipients of any ABO/Rh type in an emergency. It is called the universal donor type.

problems.subject: biology
problems.title: Monohybrid ratio
problems.statement: Two heterozygous individuals $Aa\times Aa$ are crossed, where $A$ is completely dominant over $a$. What is the expected phenotypic ratio?
problems.hint: Draw a $2\times2$ Punnett square.
problems.solution: The Punnett square gives $AA:Aa:aA:aa=1:2:1$ by genotype. Since $AA$ and $Aa$ both show the dominant phenotype, the phenotypic ratio is $3:1$.

problems.subject: biology
problems.title: Energy along a food chain
problems.statement: A grassland food chain is grass → grasshopper → frog → snake. If the grass contains $1000\ \text{kJ}$ of energy and $10\%$ is transferred at each step, how much energy reaches the snake?
problems.hint: Apply the $10\%$ rule at each transfer.
problems.solution: Grass $1000\ \text{kJ}\to$ grasshopper $100\ \text{kJ}\to$ frog $10\ \text{kJ}\to$ snake $1\ \text{kJ}$. The snake receives $1\ \text{kJ}$.

problems.subject: biology
problems.title: A carrier mother
problems.statement: Red–green colour blindness is X-linked recessive. A carrier mother and a father with normal colour vision have children. What proportion of their sons is expected to be colour-blind?
problems.hint: Sons receive their X chromosome from their mother.
problems.solution: Let the mother be $X^CX^c$ and the father $X^CY$. A son receives $Y$ from his father and either $X^C$ or $X^c$ from his mother, each with probability $\tfrac12$. So $50\%$ of sons are expected to be colour-blind. Daughters receive $X^C$ from their father, so none are colour-blind, though half are carriers.

problems.subject: biology
problems.title: Hardy–Weinberg heterozygotes
problems.statement: In a population at Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium, the frequency of allele $A$ is $p=0.8$ and of allele $a$ is $q=0.2$. What is the expected frequency of heterozygotes?
problems.hint: Heterozygote frequency is $2pq$.
problems.solution: $2pq=2(0.8)(0.2)=0.32$, so $32\%$ of the population is expected to be heterozygous.

problems.subject: biology
problems.title: Base composition
problems.statement: A double-stranded DNA molecule contains $30\%$ adenine. What percentage of its bases is guanine?
problems.hint: Use complementary base pairing: $A=T$ and $G=C$.
problems.solution: Since $A=30\%$, thymine is also $30\%$. Together they make $60\%$, leaving $40\%$ for G and C. Because $G=C$, guanine is $20\%$.
